_comment: Every place the pipeline has to touch Google Flow's UI, in one file, because
Flow is a Radix SPA with hashed class names and it WILL move. When a run
fails with 'prompt box not found' or 'click target not found', this is the
file to edit — nothing else needs to change.
How to find a replacement: open the Flow project, right-click the control,
Inspect, and prefer in this order — a data- attribute, an aria-label, a
stable semantic tag. Never a hashed class name; those change on every Flow
deploy. `generate_text` matches on visible button text and is the most
durable of the three, which is why it is the default rather than a fallback.
`plate_input` is the file input behind Flow's reference-image control. It is
usually hidden and often only mounted once you have opened that panel, so if
set_image reports 'no file input matched', open the panel by hand once and
re-run — the pipeline is not able to click a control it cannot see.
`reference_clear` is the button that REMOVES an already-attached reference
image — the ✕ on the chip, or whatever Flow renders in its place. It is null
until somebody inspects the panel once and fills it in, and a null is
reported rather than worked around, because the failure it causes is silent:
emptying the file input does not clear the chips Flow has already rendered,
so one chained clip's carry frame rides along into the clip after next and
that clip is generated from two references, one of them stale. Everything
still runs; the sequence is just subtly wrong. `video veo` prints a warning
on every chained run until this is set.
`reference_panel` is the control that OPENS that panel, if Flow only mounts
the file input once it has been opened. Also optional: leave it null and open
the panel by hand once per session instead.
